elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: IBM's only Agreement-level termination right in the cited text is for uncured material breach (§3.3); its only unilateral exit is the §3.2 auto-renewal election given at least 90 days before the end of the then-current term, which is natural-term non-renewal (assessed under RENEWAL), not a mid-term convenience right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Edited §3.4(b): "paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, capped at three months' charges for terminated Services." The cap attaches to all Attachment A / Service Option Attachment early termination charges, not merely recurring ones.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: No IBM convenience right exists mid-term: §3.3 permits IBM to terminate only for uncured material breach, and §3.2 permits IBM only to elect non-renewal effective at the end of the then-current term. The mapping's cited quote (§3.3 breach clause) is imprecise evidence, but the substance — absence of any IBM mid-term convenience right — holds on the rendered text.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: §3.2: IBM must notify "in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term ... that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment." That is the only IBM no-cause exit and it carries a 90-day notice floor.

verification.notes: Fallback is complete: Customer keeps a one-month convenience exit (better than the 60–90 day ceiling), early termination charges are now capped at three months' charges for the terminated Services, and IBM has no mid-term convenience right — its only no-cause exit is the §3.2 term-end non-renewal on 90 days' notice. Preferred fails on two elements: there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid charges on convenience termination, and the notice construct (one month's notice effective only at a calendar month end) can push the exit well past 30 days. To reach preferred the drafter would need to insert a refund of prepaid charges for the post-termination period and replace "at least one month's prior written notice ... at the end of any calendar month" with a flat "thirty (30) days' prior written notice". Minimality fails. Operations 1 and 2 only relocate and duplicate the words "for convenience": the original sentence already read "... or any Service Option Attachment (with the exception of ...) for convenience at the end of any calendar month", so the convenience qualifier already governed both branches. The fallback element it was mapped to was already met, making the edit a cosmetic paraphrase that duplicates an operative term outside the only necessary change. Repair by reverting to the original wording of the opening clause and keeping only the §3.4(b) cap. Intent is preserved: the one-month notice, the calendar month-end effective date, the prerequisite-attachment carve-out and the §3.3 proviso barring IBM from recovering §3.4(b) charges after its own breach all survive without contradiction, and the cap creates no dangling cross-reference to Attachment A. Deviation status is correct because the pre-edit clause failed the fallback on the uncapped Attachment A early termination charges, but the exposure is narrow (a fee cap only, with the Customer exit and the absence of a Vendor mid-term convenience right already in place), so severity is better characterised as medium.

verification.notes: Fallback is position-complete: a single inserted sentence supplies the three-month ceiling, exclusivity, and the resulting limitation of any Customer-payable liquidated amount to the early-termination charge. Preferred is not met and is correctly not claimed: Section 3.4(b) still conditions convenience termination on payment of early termination charges. Minimality holds. The drafter added one sentence and deleted nothing, preserving Section 3.4(b) and the Section 3.3 cross-reference to "the early termination charges described in Section 3.4(b)", so no dangling reference arises. No survival tail, procedure, expense language, or other extra requirement was added, and the cap is set exactly at the fallback threshold rather than above it. Intent is preserved: the Customer-favourable Section 3.3 carve-out (IBM cannot recover early termination charges where IBM is the breaching party), the 30-day/7-business-day cure mechanics, the prerequisite Service Option Attachment exception, and the end-of-month timing all survive without contradiction; the new sentence only ceilings and de-duplicates amounts fixed in Attachment A. Residual (rationale-level, not a defect requiring repair): "three (3) months' charges" does not name the measuring period or charge type (e.g., "the monthly recurring charges payable for the terminated Services averaged over the three months preceding termination"). If precision is wanted in negotiation, tighten the base, but as drafted the ceiling is operative and enforceable against the Attachment A amounts.
